title: South China Sea Clash Sparks Diplomatic Crisis at ASEAN Manila Summit
excerpt: A violent encounter between Chinese and Philippine forces at Second Thomas Shoal has triggered ambassador summonings and drawn sharp international rebukes, overshadowing the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting.
body:
A violent confrontation between Chinese Coast Guard personnel and Philippine navy forces in the South China Sea has erupted into a diplomatic crisis, casting a shadow over the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Manila this week.

The Philippine military said on Monday that a Chinese Coast Guard rigid-hull inflatable boat carrying eight personnel approached its grounded warship on Second Thomas Shoal. When two Philippine navy boats moved to intercept, Chinese personnel "reacted violently and aggressively by striking Philippine navy personnel with a wooden baton," according to the Armed Forces of the Philippines. A navy rubber boat was also damaged.

China's Coast Guard offered a starkly different account, accusing Philippine vessels of ignoring warnings and attacking its officers first with "paddles, wooden poles and other implements." Both sides released video footage supporting their versions.

Ambassadors Summoned as Tensions Escalate

The fallout was swift. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. summoned China's ambassador in Manila on Tuesday, hours after Manila's envoy in Beijing was similarly called in. The Philippine foreign ministry called the incident an "unacceptable" act of violence warranting diplomatic action.

"Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr."

"China's troubling pattern of provocation against lawful Philippine maritime operations undermines regional peace and stability."

— U.S. State Department spokesperson

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi pushed back sharply. In talks with ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn, Wang said "certain forces within the Philippine military and police deliberately engaged in provocations" that served the interests of "external forces." Beijing added that ASEAN was not the appropriate forum for bilateral maritime disputes.

Rubio, Wang Hold 90-Minute Meeting

Despite the tensions, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Wang held a 90-minute meeting on Wednesday, discussing the groundwork for Chinese President Xi Jinping's planned visit to Washington in September, according to Reuters. They also discussed trade, Taiwan, and areas for potential cooperation.

Rubio had earlier published an opinion piece in Philippine newspapers warning of "dire new threats" if South China Sea waters fell "under the control of a power willing to use commerce as a geopolitical weapon." He reiterated that the 2016 arbitral ruling invalidating China's sweeping sovereignty claims was "final and binding." China does not recognize the ruling.

"The countries of the region have a choice to make about how we all respond to that."

— Penny Wong, Australian Foreign Minister

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong called the altercation "risky and destabilising," while Canada's Anita Anand termed it "troubling." Australia also announced a $6.7 million drone package for the Philippine Coast Guard. China's foreign ministry hit back, saying Australia had "no right to intervene" in the South China Sea.

India Deepens ASEAN Engagement Through Quad

India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar attended the Manila meetings on July 22-23, participating in ASEAN-India, East Asia Summit, and ASEAN Regional Forum sessions. He also joined Rubio and counterparts from Australia and Japan for a Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting — a grouping Beijing has criticized as "Cold War-like."

The Ministry of External Affairs said the visit underscored "India's deepening engagement with ASEAN under the Act East Policy," noting that 2026 has been designated the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation. For the Indian diaspora across Southeast Asia, the escalating tensions carry direct economic implications — the region is a major oil importer heavily exposed to supply disruptions, compounded by the concurrent U.S.-Iran conflict.

What's Next

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov confirmed he would meet Rubio in Manila on Thursday to discuss the Ukraine war. The ASEAN meetings will also address Myanmar's civil war, now in its fifth year with an estimated 100,000 dead.

The Second Thomas Shoal — within the Philippines' 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone but 1,300 km from mainland China — remains the most volatile flashpoint. A June 2024 confrontation at the same site left one Filipino sailor with a severed thumb and led to a provisional understanding on resupply missions. Whether that fragile arrangement survives the latest escalation remains to be seen.
